The trigger was single-stock: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive about two weeks after he resigned, saying it had received input from senior US government levels, and President Trump said he had 'convinced' the board; NVDA rose 31.48%, its best day since 2003, taking its market value to roughly $4 trillion from about $3 trillion at Friday's close (CNBC and Fortune, 23 November). Breadth inverted from Friday: 417 advancers to 83 decliners with 10 of 11 sectors higher - Technology +8.97%, Consumer Discretionary +3.97%, Industrials +3.90% against Consumer Staples -0.09% and Energy -1.06% - but equal-weight RSP rose only 2.59%, 214bp less than the cap-weighted index, so the recovery was as concentrated as the decline was. Credit joined the rally, HYG +0.25%, JNK +0.28% and LQD +0.23%, though the ICE BofA high-yield spread's latest dated print is 3.76% as of 20 November, up from 3.52%. CME FedWatch put a 25bp hike at the 9 December FOMC at about 98%, with 50bp largely priced out. S&P Global's flash November PMIs missed: composite 54.6 from 55.9, the slowest private-sector expansion in four months, services 54.7 against 55.6-55.7 expected and manufacturing 54.5 from 54.9. WTI fell 3.88% to $80.17, its lowest close since 26 August, on Russia-Ukraine peace-deal progress. dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Tuesday 24 November 2026 on contracts drafted by the GitHub Actions fetch job from Monday 23 November's close, which had already landed when this session started - no wait was needed. Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-23. The blindness rule cost less than usual this session because 23 November was itself a Monday with a full cash session: the news-log entries dated 23 November (the pre-open futures surge, Asian stabilisation measures, CrowdStrike's offer for Zscaler, gold's rebound and oil's slide) are all dated on S and were used. What was excluded: everything dated 24 November, including Saxo Bank's 24 November Options Brief (which reports the one-day volatility gauge falling 48.01% to 26.69), the four news-log entries dated 24 November, and a financefeeds reading of 6.35% one-month EUR/USD implied volatility dated 24 November. Three sources the 20 November board had to exclude as after-S are used here because they are dated 21-23 November: Saxo's 23 November Options Brief, FXEmpire's week-ahead calendar updated 23 November 05:03 GMT, and the Thanksgiving seasonality work summarised from BofA's Stephen Suttmeier.

The session itself was the sharpest single-day risk reset in this ledger's record and it reset three of the six stretch readings at once. The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17 (ES=F +4.31%), the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% and the Nasdaq-100 cash index 6.86% (NQ=F +6.08%), all on Nvidia's board reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive - NVDA +31.48%, its best day since 2003, roughly $1 trillion of market value added back. Equities' stretch score moved from -3 (extreme-down) to -1 (neutral), the Nasdaq-100's from -3 to -1 and the Russell's from -1 to 0; gold's improved from -5 to -3 but stayed extreme-down; bonds stayed at exactly 0; and the dollar went the other way, from +4 to +5, now the only extreme reading left and the most extended the dollar has been in this ledger, with all four price-based components firing and the close sitting exactly at its 252-session closing high of 104.306.

Two sigma inputs are carried rather than dated on S, and both are documented in their sigmaSource fields with the direction of the error stated. The Russell's RVX is carried one session from the 20 November close of 36.88 because no 23 November value was obtainable; with the VIX down 25.83% on the day that figure very likely overstates small-cap volatility and widens the Russell's bands, but it does not change the stretch label (0 on 36.88, -1 on a VIX-sized decline to about 27 - both neutral). The dollar's EUR/USD one-month implied volatility of 6.10% is carried from 13 November and is now 6 sessions stale; the stretch components are identical at the 6.41% alternative reading, so the +5 does not rest on the stale value. Bonds' TLT implied-volatility carry of 15 is now 40 sessions stale and is the one input in this document that is clearly wrong in level rather than just old: the MOVE index rose 10.69% to 106.31 on 20 November, so a sigma of 15 narrows the Treasury bands (1D 0.47%) more than the real volatility justifies. MOVE is a basis-point yield-volatility gauge and cannot be converted to a ZN=F percentage sigma without inventing a conversion, so the carry stands and the distortion is recorded rather than fixed.

Bonds resolve to no-call at all three horizons. ZN=F closed 106.609375, to the tick the same price as on 20 November - a genuinely 0.00% session - and the asset has no dated positioning figure, no sentiment survey, no breadth analogue, no earnings analogue and no seasonality statistic available for this window, so only four to five of twelve categories carry a directional fact and all three horizons fall below the live gate of 7. That is the gate working as designed, not a gap being papered over; the alternative would have been inventing direction for six neutral categories.

context.newsLog is written here as the four flat news-log records dated 23 November rather than as {id, data} wrappers. Writing the flat records matches the shape the dedupe matches on (date + event text) and the panel shows four.

mtl.drivers.check_vote_signs flags nine of this document's Cross-asset votes - equities h1/h5, gold h1/h5, iwm h1/h5, qqq h1/h5 as 'bull via oil but corrOil negative', and dollar h1 as 'bear via oil but corrOil positive'. Those flags are false positives this session, and the reason is worth recording: the helper tests only the sign of each asset's measured oil correlation against the side of the vote, which implicitly assumes crude ROSE. On 23 November WTI FELL 3.88% to $80.17, its lowest close since 26 August, so a negative correlation to a falling driver is a positive for the asset and a positive correlation to a falling driver is a negative - exactly the votes written here. The helper is not wired into publish.py, build.py, verify.py or any test, so it gated nothing; verify_document returned no errors. It would need the direction of the driver's move, not just the correlation's sign, to be correct on a down-oil session.
